TipTopShop — Shopify Replication & Improvements Proposal

Client: TipTopShop (tiptopshop.com.au), Casio watches sold online in Australia
Prepared by: LitOS/LitGroup  ·  Date: October 7, 2026
$1,500Total estimate (§4)
50h$30/hrRebuild on Shopify with the changes in §1
EllaTheme, free through our partnership (§3)

This proposal covers replicating tiptopshop.com.au from Magento to Shopify. Along the way we suggest a few improvements, based on what we saw on the current site. This document shows what we'd replicate, the improvements we suggest, the theme we'd use, and the cost.

1

What we found on the current site

AreaWhat we see todayWhat we'd do
HeaderNo wishlist icon (§1.1)Add a "Wishlist" icon next to the cart
SubmenuCentred text in a narrow box, names wrap onto two lines (§1.1)One line per item, left-aligned, lighter dividers
ColoursOrange-brown, teal, blue and red used side by side (§1.2)One palette taken from your header
HomepageTwo sidebars, product grid and a long text block. Reads like a catalogue (§1.3)No sidebars. Hero, then categories, then products, then a short text
Style errorsSearch button, tablet layout, filter panel and price tags (§1.4)Rebuilt clean in the new theme, tested on desktop, tablet and phone
Collection pageFilters sit at the bottom of the page on mobile (§1.5)"Filter" button at the top that opens a popup
Product pageColours off-palette, no related products (§1.6)Match the palette and add "Related products"

1.1 Header, wishlist and submenu

TodayThe names are centred and wrap onto two lines, for example "Casio Baby-G Watches". The orange dividers are heavy.

ReferenceTarget style. Each name fits on one line, text is left-aligned and the dividers are light. We'd build the submenu this way.

Your site uses a wishlist, so we'd put a "Wishlist" icon in the header next to the cart. Shopify has no built-in wishlist. Ella includes a wishlist heart, but its maker recommends an app for lists tied to customer accounts, so we'd test it on your setup first (§2, question 1).

1.2 Colours

TodayYour header is the base palette: cream background, slate-blue buttons and badge, orange and yellow from the logo.

TodayThe red boxes mark colours that don't belong: a teal heading and blue slider arrows. We'd bring both into the header palette.

1.3 Homepage

TodayThe red boxes mark the left banner column and the right trust column. Most of the page goes to side banners and product cards. The first product also shows a broken image.

We'd remove both sidebars and use this order:

#BlockWhat goes in it
1HeroOne large banner, with G-Shock and Baby-G as the lead brands
2Shop by categoryTiles built from today's left-column banners: Latest Releases, Clearance, Kids, Pro Trek
3Featured productsSame products, in a cleaner grid
4Just arrivedSlider, with arrows in the main palette
5Short welcome textThe long text cut to three points: same-day dispatch before 2pm, 365-day returns, full warranty

The orange bar under the header already shows delivery, returns, warranty and warehouse. We'd keep it and add the Casio "Authorised Online Sales Partner" badge and "350,000+ orders shipped" to it or to the footer, so the right column's trust points aren't lost.

1.4 Style errors

TodayThe search button is green with an angled edge and a shadow. The desktop header uses a slate-blue button, so the two don't match.

TodayOn a tablet the sidebars squeeze the product cards. Look at the red price tags: sizes differ and the pointed ends overlap the text below. The first product again shows a broken image.

TodayIn the red boxes, the Casio badge touches the "Category" box and the Category and Price boxes overlap.

TodayThe arrows point to the line under the price tags. It breaks between the cards instead of running as one continuous line.

These come from the old Magento theme. We don't repair them one by one. We build the search box, price tags and filter panel fresh in Ella, then check every page on desktop, tablet and phone.

1.5 Collection page and filter

TodayOn a phone, the filters (Category, Price, Manufacturer, Color) come after all the products. A shopper has to scroll the whole list to find them.

Filters are what shoppers need most on a collection page, so we'd move them to the top. A "Filter" button sits above the products and opens a popup. We build it with Shopify's free Search & Discovery app. Ella supports checkbox, swatch and rectangle filter styles, so colour can show as swatches.

1.6 Product page

ReferenceSupplied with the brief, not the live site. Look at the orange "Add to cart" button, the heart beside it and the delivery and warranty panel below. We'd use the same palette and add a "Related products" row under the product.

Open questions

#QuestionWhy it matters
1Should customers be able to save a wishlist that stays in their account?Decides if Ella's wishlist is enough or a paid wishlist app is needed (your account).
2Can you send the logo file and brand colour codes?We take colours from the screenshots otherwise. Exact codes avoid a mismatch.
3Do you agree with the homepage order in §1.3, and who writes the shorter welcome text?We can cut it to three points for your approval, or you send the copy.
4Which filters stay on the collection page?Each filter needs matching product data on Shopify.
3

Theme

We recommend Ella by HaloThemes. It is free to you through our partnership. It covers what this brief needs: a wishlist heart, several mega menu layouts, product card layouts, and filter styles with colour swatches.

Who configures what

Payment is set up by you in your Shopify admin. We guide you and verify the result, but we don't enter the credentials. They give access to your money, so they stay with the account holder.

ItemYou doWe do
Payment providerOpen the account, enter the credentials, run the first live orderRecommend a provider, give you a step-by-step guide, test checkout
